methodological_rigor.justification: The study assembles a very large multicohort cfMeDIP-seq compendium (n=1,294) processed through a uniform pipeline (MEDIPIPE), systematically benchmarks six normalization strategies, applies ComBat-seq+DESeq2 batch correction, and uses an in-silico PBL depletion strategy to control a well-known confounder. Classifier development uses nested cross-validation with PCA fit on training folds only to prevent leakage, external validation in 220 independent samples (including 3 unseen cancer types), and formal power analyses (univariate pwr.t.test; multivariate PERMANOVA simulation). Statistical choices are generally appropriate (Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's and BH correction, permutation-based enrichment, FDR-adjusted DMR calling with |log2FC|>1, FDR<0.05) and effect-size thinking is used for power. Important limitations acknowledged in-text: age/sex missing for >240 samples (excluded from covariate adjustment for AML, bladder, renal, brain), SE vs PE batch effects remain despite correction, data collection/analysis not blinded or randomized, class imbalance handled via down-sampling (reduces training data), and no pre-registration or pre-specified primary endpoints.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a diagnostic biomarker development and classifier validation study compiling case-control style comparisons (cancer vs healthy) across nine cohorts with an independent validation set, which maps to Oxford CEBM 3b (individual case-control / diagnostic case series across cohorts; not a prospective diagnostic accuracy study in a consecutive screening population, which would be 2b or 1b). Clinical relevance is high: multi-cancer early detection is a major unmet need; endpoints are directly diagnostic (sensitivity at 99%/95% specificity benchmarked against GRAIL's methylation assay and cfMethyl-seq), and the integrated methylome+fragmentome from a single cfMeDIP-seq assay is a plausible, cost-reducing translational path. The LFS subgroup analyses (previvor/survivor/positive) add relevance for hereditary cancer surveillance.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the most applicable standard given the central deliverable is a multivariable prediction model for cancer vs healthy and cancer-type classification; REMARK elements are also relevant for the DMR biomarker discovery. The manuscript reports participants, predictors, model specification, internal validation (nested CV), external validation (TCGE-CFMe-INSPIRE + TCGE-CFMe-HCC), handling of missing covariates, class imbalance, and sample-flow (100+123 primary and 19+106 validation exclusions explicitly stated). Key TRIPOD gaps: no pre-registration, no explicit calibration assessment (only discrimination via AUC and sensitivity at fixed specificity), no decision-curve or clinical utility analysis, and limited reporting of model-coefficient-level transparency. Data/code posture is strong: MEDIPIPE pipeline is a published open resource; a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.15191455) hosts source data; source data per figure is listed; however, trained classifier weights and ML pipeline code availability are not explicitly described in the retained text.

novelty_literature.justification: Primary novelty is empirical and methodological: this is to my knowledge the largest uniformly reprocessed cfMeDIP-seq compendium (1,294 samples across 11 cancer types + LFS) and the first systematic pancancer integration of methylation with fragmentomic features (5' end motifs, DELFI-style ratios, nucleosome footprinting, insert size) derived from the same cfMeDIP-seq assay. Individual components are not new (DELFI, Jiang end-motifs, Snyder nucleosome footprinting, cfMeDIP-seq by Shen et al. 2018 are all cited and leveraged), and multi-cancer detection has been established by GRAIL/CCGA and cfMethyl-seq, limiting conceptual novelty. The pancancer DMR catalog (14,202 common hyper-DMRs) and the DNASE1L3-linked motif analysis across tumor types extend prior single-cancer work, representing solid directional novelty rather than paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear logical flow from data curation → confounder mitigation → DMR identification → fragmentomics → integrated classification → subtype classification. The abstract is concise, quantitatively grounded (1,074 primary + 220 validation, 14,202 DMRs), and accurately reflects content. Figure legends are detailed with explicit sample counts and box-plot conventions, improving standalone interpretability. Minor issues: dense acronym load (cfMeDIP, DMR, PBL, FS, DELFI, NMF, mAUC) occasionally impedes flow for non-specialist readers; some Methods subsections are long and could be subdivided; a few sentences in Results blur Methods-level detail (e.g., SE/PE batch correction logic appears in both Methods and Results).

key_strengths: Largest uniformly reprocessed pancancer cfMeDIP-seq compendium to date (n=1,294) with explicit batch, PBL, age and sex confounder mitigation

Rigorous ML workflow: nested CV, PCA fit only on training folds, independent external validation (220 samples including 3 unseen cancer types), formal univariate and PERMANOVA-based multivariate power analyses

Integrated methylome + fragmentome (5' end motifs, DELFI ratios, nucleosome footprints, insert size) from a single assay with benchmarking against GRAIL and cfMethyl-seq (89.6% sensitivity at 99% specificity in primary PE)
Public resource contribution: MEDIPIPE pipeline, Zenodo-deposited source data, per-figure source data, 14,202 pancancer hyper-DMR catalog plus cancer-specific DMRs for 11 cancer types
LFS previvor/survivor/positive subgroup analysis adds hereditary-surveillance relevance beyond standard case-control framing
key_concerns: Age/sex missing for >240 samples, forcing exclusion of AML, bladder, renal, and brain cancers from covariate-adjusted DMR analyses; residual confounding cannot be fully excluded
Intrinsic SE vs PE differences persist after ComBat-seq correction and were handled by processing streams separately rather than resolved; limits cross-stream generalizability claims
TRIPOD/REMARK gaps: no protocol pre-registration, no calibration assessment or decision-curve analysis, model-coefficient transparency and ML code availability not explicitly stated in retained text
HCC validation healthy controls show protocol-driven 5' motif baseline shift that degrades motif-containing classifiers, raising preanalytical generalizability concerns across labs

Data collection and analysis not blinded; class-imbalance addressed by random down-sampling (reduces effective training data); some per-type validation sample sizes very small (e.g., melanoma n=9 with 33.3% accuracy)
Novelty is strong but incremental over GRAIL/Galleri, cfMethyl-seq, DELFI, and Jiang end-motif work; mechanistic DNASE1L3 claim remains correlational
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically solid, resource-level pancancer liquid biopsy study with external validation and multiple confounder controls, placing it plausibly at a top-tier venue (Tier 1, e.g., Nature Methods/Communications/Cancer Cell level); minor revisions are warranted around TRIPOD-aligned calibration reporting, SE/PE harmonization limits, and preanalytical protocol effects observed in the HCC healthy controls.
